transcript:
Header: 2025-12-09 15:00 PST | Duration: ~51 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Kim, Priya Shah, Luca Moretti (Redwood) — Dr. Hannah Liu, Marco Alvarez, Sasha Petrov, Ellen Park (Evergreen Diagnostics)

Summary (auto): walk-through of Redwood Console and API flags for request logging, demo of redaction rules and retention toggle, Q&A on SOC2/KMS and network isolation. Agreed follow-ups: security pack + sample retention config + pilot kickoff scheduling.

00:00:04 Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thank you for joining, I'm Jordan, AE on the account, with Priya our SE and Luca from product. how's everyone doing?
00:00:10 Dr. Hannah Liu: Good thanks. busy but excited — we wanted to make sure we cover the data handling pieces end to end.
00:00:18 Marco Alvarez: Quick preface: we're regulated, PHI/PII in many payloads, so we need to lock down what gets logged and how long it's kept.
00:00:27 Jordan Kim: Absolutely, that's the center of today's demo. we'll show Console toggles, the API-level flags, and some Optimize recommendations to reduce logging surface.
00:00:38 Priya Shah: Quick note, I'll demo a live session in the Console and then switch to API examples. If transcription gets a little messy you'll see some typos — audio from my side is a little echoey.
00:00:48 Sasha Petrov: no problem.

00:02:10 Priya Shah: Opening the Console — Home view, then Privacy controls -> Request storage. you'll see three modes: Ephemeral (no request stored), Session-ephemeral (store cache but redact full text), and Persisted (store requests to S3-like bucket).
00:02:34 Ellen Park: When you say 'redact full text' that means we can keep telemetry but strip identifiable fields?
00:02:40 Priya Shah: Right — we have field-based redaction rules. you can add regexes or selected keys to redact at ingestion time. for structured JSON we also support path-based masks, e.g., patient.ssn or records[*].email.
00:02:59 Dr. Hannah Liu: are redaction rules run client-side or server-side? we need to ensure PII doesn't leave our VPC unencrypted.
00:03:10 Priya Shah: They're server-side in the Redwood runtime. For Private deployments we can run the same redaction pipeline inside your VPC/on-prem; for Hosted we transit over TLS and we have optional in-flight tokenization. Regarding encryption, all persisted buckets are encrypted with customer-managed keys when KMS is enabled.
00:03:33 Marco Alvarez: do you support HSM-backed KMS or bring-your-own-key?
00:03:37 Priya Shah: Yes — BYOK via AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault. HSM integrations can be arranged for Private installs — Luca can speak to this.
00:03:47 Luca Moretti: For enterprise Private we provide a connector to on-prem HSMs and can configure rotation policies — it's part of the platform package.

00:05:12 Dr. Hannah Liu: Can you show how to toggle request logging at the API level — we might want dev team to always log but production to be ephemeral.
00:05:20 Priya Shah: Sure — switching to API examples. There's a request-level header x-redwood-request-retention: ephemeral|session|persist. In our SDKs it's a parameter on the call: { retention: 'ephemeral' }. We'll show Postman example in the doc after the call.
00:05:41 Marco Alvarez: If someone forgets the header, is there a default policy per model or per route?
00:05:47 Priya Shah: Good question. You set a global org default and then route overrides. We also support per-api-key policies so service accounts can be locked down.

00:07:05 Sasha Petrov: What about audit logs? we need to know who accessed stored requests and when.
00:07:12 Priya Shah: Audit logs capture read/write events, identity via SSO/SAML/SCIM integration, and can be forwarded to your SIEM (CloudWatch, Splunk). We keep an immutable append-only audit trail for admin actions on retention settings.
00:07:29 Dr. Hannah Liu: That helps for compliance. Do you record query text in the audits?
00:07:35 Priya Shah: Audit entries include metadata — who changed the setting, what value, timestamp. The raw request text is only in persisted storage if retention mode is persisted and not redacted.

00:09:00 Priya Shah: Now demoing redaction rule creation — I'll add a rule to mask fields matching regex for phone and SSN, show preview on sample payload. Preview shows redacted output with [REDACTED] tokens.
00:09:25 Marco Alvarez: Is the preview deterministic? we need reproducible redactions for debugging.
00:09:30 Priya Shah: Yes deterministic and we log the rule version so you can trace when a change affected outputs.

00:11:15 Jordan Kim: Quick interject — on the topic of telemetry you mentioned earlier, we also provide token-level telemetry (latency/cost) without full request storage. Optimize uses that to recommend batching or caching and can flag high-entropy prompts that blow up token costs.
00:11:33 Dr. Hannah Liu: Can Optimize recommendations be applied automatically or are they suggestions only?
00:11:38 Luca Moretti: Currently suggestions only, but with an approval workflow you can auto-apply safe configs like batching thresholds and prefix caching. We don't change model output; we only alter runtime config to adjust cost/latency.

00:13:05 Marco Alvarez: If we turn on ephemeral for production, can we still collect metrics for QoS and debugging?
00:13:12 Priya Shah: Yes — we keep aggregated metrics (per-route latency histograms, token usage) even when request bodies are ephemeral. You can opt into minimal request IDs and error traces without storing request text.
00:13:26 Sasha Petrov: How do you handle transcripts from voice inputs — they may contain PHI that we can't persist.
00:13:33 Priya Shah: We treat audio similarly; transcription results are subject to the same retention settings. You can also configure automatic redaction post-transcription.

00:15:00 Ellen Park: Network isolation — does Redwood's Hosted plan ever touch our private datasets if we enable persisted?
00:15:08 Priya Shah: For Hosted persisted storage data is stored in our customer buckets; we support customer-managed buckets (S3) where your data resides in your account with access policies. For full isolation you can use Redwood Private with a control plane in your VPC.
00:15:25 Marco Alvarez: Ok, so for now we prefer customer-managed S3 + BYOK.

00:16:38 Dr. Hannah Liu: Let's talk deletion and retention windows. We need a legal hold capability and quick delete ops for e-data requests.
00:16:45 Priya Shah: Retention windows are configurable per route with minimum 0 days up to years. We have a 'legal hold' flag that prevents deletion until cleared, with audit trail. Deletes are soft then hard after a policy TTL, and we support immediate wipes for sensitive records with a compliance log.
00:17:07 Marco Alvarez: How fast is hard delete? i.e., if stored on S3, do you remove objects immediately?
00:17:12 Priya Shah: When using customer-managed buckets you can configure lifecycle rules and we provide a deletion API that issues object deletion and confirms via audit. For Redwood-managed storage we do a guaranteed hard-delete within 24 hours for requested deletions (enterprise SLA varies).

00:19:20 Priya Shah: switching back to UI — showing a policy roll-out screen. You can canary retention changes to a subset of keys or api keys and monitor regressions.
00:19:36 Dr. Hannah Liu: The canary is useful. if a policy causes redaction too aggressively that breaks evaluation, can we roll back instantly?
00:19:42 Priya Shah: Yes — rollbacks are immediate. we also keep a pre/post sample diff so you can validate.

00:21:10 Jordan Kim: Pricing question often comes up — does enabling persisted storage add to cost?
00:21:17 Priya Shah: Persisted storage is priced separately based on GB-month and request throughput; redaction adds marginal compute. We'll include estimated costs in the follow-up pricing sheet.

00:22:55 Sasha Petrov: Security specifics — do you support SSO and granular RBAC so only specific users can access persisted requests?
00:23:02 Priya Shah: Yes SSO via SAML/OIDC; RBAC roles include Viewer/Analyst/Admin and a specific 'Request Accessor' role that can view persisted requests if policy allows. Access flows can be gated behind approval workflows.

00:24:40 Ellen Park: About logs forwarded to SIEM — can we ship raw logs or only metadata? sometimes compliance requires raw event ingestion.
00:24:48 Priya Shah: We can forward both. For Hosted customers we can forward events to your SIEM over a secure forwarder. For persistent storage we recommend customer-managed sinks.

00:26:30 Marco Alvarez: Are there examples of regex rules that accidentally over-redact? we want to avoid false positives removing clinical terms.
00:26:39 Priya Shah: Great callout. we recommend whitelist examples and test harnesses; we provide a 'test suite' where you run your dataset through redaction rules and inspect diffs. Also the rule engine supports allowlists and word-boundary anchors to avoid overreach.

00:28:00 Priya Shah: Now API demo — sending a sample request with x-redwood-request-retention: session, payload includes PHI fields. Show response (redacted in logs) and show audit entry created.
00:28:15 Dr. Hannah Liu: The transcript shows [REDACTED] in logs which is good. in practice how do Devs debug if logs are redacted?
00:28:23 Priya Shah: We recommend a dev-only API key that uses session persistence in a dev account, or you can enable masked logs (hashes of PII) that let you correlate without revealing raw data.

00:30:40 Jordan Kim: Customer question on SLA — do retention features affect latency or our SLOs?
00:30:46 Priya Shah: Redaction processing is lightweight at ingest; for extremely large documents we stream redaction and it's pipelined. We have SLOs and can provision dedicated capacity for heavy redaction workloads.

00:33:00 Marco Alvarez: What's the plan for versioning redaction rules? we need to audit which rule set applied to a given request historically.
00:33:06 Priya Shah: Each rule has an immutable version ID and we store the rule version ID with the request metadata. When you run an audit you can query by rule version.

00:34:50 Dr. Hannah Liu: Any notable limitations on the hosted side vs private for our use-case?
00:34:57 Luca Moretti: Hosted is faster to onboard but for aggressive compliance needs — full VPC control, private networking, and on-prem HSM — Private is recommended. Hosted supports customer-managed buckets and BYOK which covers many enterprise needs short of air-gapped.

00:36:18 Ellen Park: The team asked if we can redact partial fields — keep last 4 digits of an ID for correlation but mask the rest.
00:36:25 Priya Shah: Yes we support token-preserving redactions and format-preserving masks (e.g., keep last 4).

00:38:10 Marco Alvarez: For the pilot, can we start with logging off for prod but enable dev logging and have the ability to flip per-route?
00:38:18 Jordan Kim: Absolutely, that's a common pattern. we'll send a recommended pilot config (per-route defaults + dev keys) in the follow-up.

00:40:00 Priya Shah: Quick demo of the Optimize tab — it surfaces prompts with high token amplification and suggests caching prefixes or switching model variants to reduce logs while maintaining perf. Shows sample rule: cache prefix for patient history queries.
00:40:22 Dr. Hannah Liu: If we cache prefixes, does that change outputs in unexpected ways?
00:40:28 Luca Moretti: Shouldn't if applied correctly; caching only reuses KV cache for prefix tokens, outputs remain deterministic for same inputs. We test for semantic preservation.

00:42:05 Sasha Petrov: We're concerned about third-party access — do Redwood employees ever see persisted content?
00:42:13 Priya Shah: No, access is tightly controlled. For Hosted we treat persisted content as customer data; only authorized personnel during incident triage can access with multi-party approval and every such access is logged. For Private, we have no access to your data in the VPC.

00:44:00 Dr. Hannah Liu: Great. any regret items we should be aware of — e.g., migration pain?
00:44:07 Luca Moretti: Migration tends to be straightforward; we provide ingestion scripts and a mapping assistant for regex to path conversions. Biggest work is cataloging PII fields.

00:46:10 Jordan Kim: Time for wrap up — recap and next steps.
00:46:18 Jordan Kim: Recap: we'll send SOC2 + KMS docs, sample retention config, pricing estimate, and proposed pilot plan week of 2025-12-22. Action items assigned in the doc.
00:46:30 Dr. Hannah Liu: Sounds good. we'll review and get back on legal / procurement timelines.
00:46:38 Marco Alvarez: also confirm data residency EU requirement.
00:46:42 Jordan Kim: noted — Ellen (PM) will confirm.
00:46:50 Ellen Park: I'll follow up by EOD Friday with our residency constraint.
00:47:05 Jordan Kim: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pack.
00:47:12 Priya Shah: Thanks, bye.
00:47:15 Dr. Hannah Liu: Bye.
